In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sociality is driven by the cost of dispersal, not the benefits of philopatry.
the evolution of sociality is not driven by the costs of dispersal, but by the benefits of philopatry.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the costs of dispersal are not a sufficient condition for promoting sociality, but that kin‐discriminating mechanisms are necessary to allow the evolution of altruism in the absence of such costs.
the evolution of sociality is not driven by the costs of dispersal or the benefits of philopatry but rather by the costs of discrimination.
sociality in animals is driven by the costs of dispersal and the benefits of philopatry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the role of ecology in promoting sociality depends on the cognitive mechanisms that underpin social interactions.
kin‐discriminating mechanisms can have a major impact on the role of ecological constraints and, more broadly, on the social evolution of a population.
the evolution of sociality is not simply a matter of dispersal costs, but also depends on the cognitive abilities of the species under study.
